prompt: Build a small resolver that turns a simple class name into a fully qualified one, reporting AMBIGUOUS when two wildcard imports clash. Complete WildcardImportResolver and run the tests.
explanation: This is the compiler's own name-resolution order expressed as three checks in sequence: single-type imports, then the current package, then everything reachable through wildcards. Because the first two steps return as soon as they match, they naturally beat a wildcard, which is why importing java.util.List silences the clash. The last step must gather all the matches before deciding, since ambiguity is only visible once you know there is more than one candidate.
hints: Keep three fields: a Map from package name to the Set of classes it declares, a Map from simple name to its single-type import, and a Set of wildcard-imported packages.
Return early in resolve -- a single-type import wins outright, and so does a class in the current package.
For the wildcard step, collect every match into a Set first, then decide: none means null, one means that name, more than one means "AMBIGUOUS".
